cards.name: Outline
cards.summary: The outline (pen) settings of one shape: width, color, dash style, arrowheads, caps, joins, calligraphic nib, position relative to the fill and whether it scales with the object. It is the scripting side of the Outline Pen dialog and the Properties docker's Outline section.
use_for: set a consistent stroke weight and color on every logo element before print
turn hairlines into a fixed 0.25 mm keyline that does not scale with the artwork
add arrowheads to leader lines in an infographic or diagram
copy one shape's stroke onto many shapes (CopyAssign)
turn a stroke into a filled object for cutters or laser files (ConvertToObject)
avoid: reading outline settings off a group: read each child shape, a group has no outline of its own (unverified what a group returns)
dash patterns built by hand per shape: pick or create an OutlineStyle and assign it to Style
cards.how: Coclass with no members of its own; everything is on its default interface IVGOutline (members_on). Reach it as Shape.Outline (IVGShape.Outline) for one shape, or use ActiveSelectionRange.SetOutlineProperties (IVGShapeRange) to set many shapes at once. Width and DashDotLength are in document units (ActiveDocument.Unit). Style takes an OutlineStyle (Application.OutlineStyles or CreateOutlineStyle); StartArrow / EndArrow take an ArrowHead from Application.ArrowHeads.

key_members.name: Color
key_members.use: outline Color object; change it in place with Color.RGBAssign / CMYKAssign

key_members.name: MiterLimit
key_members.use: corner angle below which a miter join is beveled

key_members.name: Justification
key_members.use: stroke centred, inside or outside the path

key_members.name: BehindFill
key_members.use: draw the outline behind the fill so only the outer half shows

key_members.name: ScaleWithShape
key_members.use: scale the stroke width when the shape is resized

key_members.name: SetPropertiesEx
key_members.use: set width, style, color, arrows, caps, joins, nib, dash length, miter and justification in one call

key_members.name: CopyAssign
key_members.use: copy every outline setting from another Outline

key_members.name: ConvertToObject
key_members.use: Convert Outline to Object: returns the new filled shape

key_members.name: VariableWidthNodes
key_members.use: width nodes of a variable-width outline (Count 0 when the width is uniform)

gotchas: Width is in document units, so the same number means different strokes under cdrInch and cdrMillimeter: set ActiveDocument.Unit first.
ScaleWithShape is per shape: a logo scaled down for a favicon keeps its print stroke weight unless this is True.
BehindFill hides the inner half of the stroke, so the visible weight looks half of Width.
Setting Width on a shape whose Type is cdrNoOutline may not make the outline visible on its own (unverified); set Type or use SetPropertiesEx.
ConvertToObject creates a new shape and leaves the original without an outline (unverified that it also deletes the original's stroke in every case).
cards.example:
Dim s As Shape
ActiveDocument.Unit = cdrMillimeter
Set s = ActiveShape
s.Outline.Width = 0.25
s.Outline.Color.CMYKAssign 0, 0, 0, 100
s.Outline.ScaleWithShape = False
s.Outline.Justification = cdrOutlineJustificationOutside
cards.source: cdr_api_22 agent (VGCoreAuto.tlb harvest; coclass members read from the members_on interface IVGOutline)

review.changes: how: replaced ActiveSelection.Outline (unverified that a selection shape fans out) with the harvested ShapeRange.SetOutlineProperties

cards.name: OutlineStyle
cards.summary: One dash pattern (the dashed / dotted line styles in the Outline Pen style list): a count of dash-gap pairs with the length of each dash and gap. Assigning it to Outline.Style makes the stroke dashed.
use_for: dashed cut or fold lines on packaging dielines
dotted leader lines in a map or infographic
a custom brand dash pattern reused across a document
avoid: changing a style taken from Application.OutlineStyles when only one shape should change: that list is app-wide; build a private style with Application.CreateOutlineStyle
cards.how: Coclass; members are on IVGOutlineStyle. Reach it as Shape.Outline.Style, Application.OutlineStyles.Item(i), or make a new one with Application.CreateOutlineStyle(DashDotCount, DashDotLengths). Apply it by assigning it to Outline.Style.

key_members.name: DashCount
key_members.use: number of dash-gap pairs in the pattern

key_members.name: Index
key_members.use: position of the style in the application's style list

key_members.name: Enhanced
key_members.use: True when the style is an enhanced-outline dash style

gotchas: Dash and gap lengths are whole numbers; they appear to be relative to the outline width rather than absolute (unverified), so a thicker stroke stretches the pattern. For an absolute repeat use Outline.DashDotLength.
Index base for DashLength / GapLength is not documented in the harvest (unverified: 1-based like the collections).
Enhanced is a read-only flag; for an enhanced style the pattern may not be fully described by DashCount / DashLength (unverified).
cards.example:
Dim st As OutlineStyle
Set st = OutlineStyles.Item(5)
Debug.Print st.Index, st.DashCount, st.DashLength(1), st.GapLength(1)
ActiveShape.Outline.Style = st
cards.source: cdr_api_22 agent (VGCoreAuto.tlb harvest; coclass members read from the members_on interface IVGOutlineStyle)

review.changes: gotchas: reworded an invented claim that enhanced styles are read-only

cards.name: OutlineStyles
cards.summary: The application-wide list of dash styles shown in the Outline Pen style drop-down. Scripts read styles from it, add new ones and save the list so the styles appear in the UI.
use_for: install a studio dash pattern (cut line, perforation, stitch) for every designer
look up an existing dash style by position to apply it in a batch macro
avoid: a one-off dashed stroke: CreateOutlineStyle gives a private style without touching the shared list
cards.how: Coclass; members are on IVGOutlineStyles. Reach it as Application.OutlineStyles (OutlineStyles unqualified in a CorelDRAW VBA macro). Item is base 1. Add returns a new style to fill in; AddStyle copies an existing OutlineStyle into the list; Save writes the list back.

key_members.name: Add
key_members.use: append a new blank style and return it

key_members.name: AddStyle
key_members.use: append a copy of a given OutlineStyle

key_members.name: Save
key_members.use: persist changes to the style list

gotchas: The list is shared by every document and user session on the machine; Remove and Save change what other designers see.
Changes may be lost at exit unless Save is called (unverified).
Which index is the solid line is not in the harvest (unverified); look up by DashCount instead of a hard-coded index.
The type library describes this class as 'the dash style applied to an outline', but its members (Item, Count, Add, Save) make it the style list; the style on one shape is Outline.Style.
cards.example:
Dim st As OutlineStyle
For Each st In OutlineStyles
    Debug.Print st.Index, st.DashCount, st.Enhanced
Next st
Set st = OutlineStyles.AddStyle(CreateOutlineStyle(1, Array(4, 2)))
OutlineStyles.Save
cards.source: cdr_api_22 agent (VGCoreAuto.tlb harvest; coclass members read from the members_on interface IVGOutlineStyles)

review.changes: gotchas: noted the misleading harvested class description

cards.name: Page
cards.summary: One page of a CorelDRAW document: its name, size, orientation, bleed, background, layers and shapes, plus search, selection and bounding-box helpers. The scripting side of the page tabs and Layout > Page Size / Page Background.
use_for: build a multi-size social or print set by setting each page's size and name
find and replace placeholder text on a template page
fit the page to its artwork before export (Autofit)
collect the shapes on one page for a batch restyle
set bleed and background before publishing a print PDF
avoid: setting the paper name through Paper: it is read-only; use SetSize / SizeWidth / SizeHeight or SelectSize
reaching master-layer content through Shapes: use AllLayers or Document.MasterPage
cards.how: Coclass; members are on IVGPage. Reach it as ActivePage, ActiveDocument.Pages.Item(n), Pages.First / Last, or from Document.AddPages / AddPagesEx / InsertPages. Sizes and coordinates are in document units; the origin is the lower-left of the page by default and y grows upward. Call Activate before code that works through ActiveLayer / ActivePage.

key_members.name: Name
key_members.use: page name shown on the page tab

key_members.name: SetSize
key_members.use: set width and height in one call

key_members.name: SelectSize
key_members.use: apply a named preset page size, optionally landscape

key_members.name: FindShape
key_members.use: one shape by name, type or static ID (Recursive into groups)

key_members.name: TextReplace
key_members.use: find and replace text on the page

key_members.name: GetObjectsBoundingBox
key_members.use: Rect around the content (selected only / include non-printable)

key_members.name: Autofit
key_members.use: resize the page to the content on its local layers plus a margin

gotchas: All lengths follow ActiveDocument.Unit; set it before writing sizes.
Paper is read-only: the harvest description says to use SizeWidth / SizeHeight to change size.
Pages.Item(0) is the master page, not the first page; a loop from 0 touches the master.
Shapes covers the page's layers but not master-layer shapes (unverified); AllLayers includes the master layers.
Delete on the only page of a document is expected to fail (unverified).
cards.example:
Dim p As Page, r As Rect
ActiveDocument.Unit = cdrMillimeter
Set p = ActiveDocument.Pages.Item(1)
p.SetSize 210, 297
p.Bleed = 3
p.Name = "Cover"
Set r = p.GetObjectsBoundingBox(False, False)
Debug.Print p.Index, r.Width, r.Height
cards.source: cdr_api_22 agent (VGCoreAuto.tlb harvest; coclass members read from the members_on interface IVGPage)

review.changes: summary: Layout > Page Setup is not a CorelDRAW 2024 menu item; harvested items are Layout/Page Size and Layout/Page Background; key_members: Autofit scoped to local layers per harvest

cards.name: Pages
cards.summary: The collection of pages of one document, in page order. Used to count, walk and pick pages; adding pages is done on the Document.
use_for: loop over every page of a brochure to export or restyle it
jump to the first or last page of a multi-page template
check page count before a page-range export
avoid: looking for Add here: create pages with Document.AddPages, AddPagesEx or InsertPages
cards.how: Coclass; members are on IVGPages. Reach it as ActiveDocument.Pages. Item is base 1 for real pages; Item(0) returns the master page. For Each walks the pages in order.

key_members.name: Count
key_members.use: number of pages (master page not counted, unverified)

gotchas: Item(0) returns the master page (harvest description), so For i = 0 To Count touches the master.
The collection is live: deleting or inserting pages inside a For i loop shifts later indexes; loop backwards when deleting.
cards.example:
Dim p As Page
For Each p In ActiveDocument.Pages
    Debug.Print p.Index, p.Name, p.SizeWidth, p.SizeHeight
Next p
ActiveDocument.Unit = cdrPixel
Set p = ActiveDocument.AddPagesEx(1, 1080, 1350)
Debug.Print ActiveDocument.Pages.Count, ActiveDocument.Pages.Last.Index
cards.source: cdr_api_22 agent (VGCoreAuto.tlb harvest; coclass members read from the members_on interface IVGPages)

review.changes: example: AddPagesEx sizes are in document units; set cdrPixel first or the page is 1080 x 1350 of the default unit

cards.name: PageSize
cards.summary: One named paper size preset (A4, Letter, a custom 'Instagram Post' and so on) from the page-size list (Layout > Page Size). It holds the name, width and height and whether it is built in.
use_for: look up the exact dimensions of a named preset before laying out
check whether a studio's custom size is installed
remove an outdated custom size
avoid: sizing a page from this object directly: apply it with Page.SelectSize(Name, Landscape) or Page.SetSize
cards.how: Coclass; members are on IVGPageSize. Reach it as Application.PageSizes.Item(IndexOrName) or as the return value of PageSizes.Add(Name, Width, Height).

key_members.name: Name
key_members.use: preset name as shown in the size list

key_members.name: DefaultUnit
key_members.use: the unit the preset is defined in

key_members.name: BuiltIn
key_members.use: True for presets shipped with CorelDRAW

key_members.name: FixedOrientation
key_members.use: True when the preset's orientation cannot be swapped

gotchas: Width / Height are typed read-write but described as 'Gets'; writing them on a built-in preset is expected to fail (unverified).
Whether Width / Height come back in document units or in DefaultUnit is not stated in the harvest (unverified); compare against a known size such as A4 first.
Delete works only on custom presets (harvest: 'Deletes the custom paper type').
cards.example:
Dim ps As PageSize
Set ps = PageSizes.Item("A4")
Debug.Print ps.Name, ps.Width, ps.Height, ps.DefaultUnit, ps.BuiltIn
ActivePage.SelectSize ps.Name, True
cards.source: cdr_api_22 agent (VGCoreAuto.tlb harvest; coclass members read from the members_on interface IVGPageSize)

review.changes: summary: menu path corrected to harvested Layout/Page Size

cards.name: PageSizes
cards.summary: The application's list of named page size presets. Scripts enumerate it, look sizes up by name, and add custom sizes that then appear in the Layout > Page Size list.
use_for: install a studio set of social-media sizes (1080x1350, 1080x1920) as named presets
check a preset exists before calling Page.SelectSize in a template macro
avoid: a one-off page size: Page.SetSize is enough and leaves the shared list alone
cards.how: Coclass; members are on IVGPageSizes. Reach it as Application.PageSizes. Item takes an index or a name. Add(Name, Width, Height) creates a custom preset and returns it.

key_members.name: Add
key_members.use: add a custom preset with name, width and height

gotchas: Item with an unknown name raises an error (unverified); trap it or walk the list first.
Units of Add's Width / Height are not stated in the harvest (unverified: document units); check the new preset's Width afterwards.
The list is application-wide and persists for other documents.
cards.example:
Dim ps As PageSize
For Each ps In PageSizes
    If Not ps.BuiltIn Then Debug.Print ps.Name, ps.Width, ps.Height
Next ps
ActiveDocument.Unit = cdrPixel
Set ps = PageSizes.Add("IG Portrait", 1080, 1350)
cards.source: cdr_api_22 agent (VGCoreAuto.tlb harvest; coclass members read from the members_on interface IVGPageSizes)

review.changes: summary: menu path corrected to harvested Layout/Page Size

cards.name: Palette
cards.summary: One color palette (custom, fixed such as PANTONE, or the document palette): its colors, name, file and open state. Scripts read, match and edit palette colors and save palettes to .xml palette files.
use_for: build a brand palette from a list of CMYK / RGB values and save it for the team
snap arbitrary colors to the nearest brand or PANTONE swatch (MatchColor)
list the colors of a client palette for a style guide page
check a document palette for duplicate swatches
avoid: editing a fixed palette (PANTONE etc.): AddColor / RemoveColor work only on custom palettes; copy colors into a custom palette instead
Delete when you only mean to hide the palette: Delete removes the palette file; use Close
cards.how: Coclass; members are on IVGPalette. Reach it as ActiveDocument.Palette (document palette), Application.ActivePalette, Palettes.Item(IndexOrName), Palettes.Open / Create / CreateFromDocument / CreateFromSelection, or PaletteManager.GetPalette / DefaultPalette / LoadPalette.

key_members.name: Name
key_members.use: palette name (settable only on custom palettes)

key_members.name: Colors
key_members.use: all colors as a Colors collection

key_members.name: AddColor
key_members.use: append a color to a custom palette

key_members.name: MatchColor
key_members.use: index of the closest palette color

key_members.name: FindColor
key_members.use: index of a color by name

key_members.name: Save
key_members.use: write changes to the palette file

key_members.name: SaveAs
key_members.use: save to a new file and name

key_members.name: Locked
key_members.use: True when the palette cannot be edited

key_members.name: MakeDefault
key_members.use: make it the application default palette

key_members.name: Delete
key_members.use: delete the palette and its file

gotchas: Name can be set only on a custom palette (harvest description); AddColor / InsertColor / RemoveColor are described as custom-palette operations.
Delete removes the palette file from disk, not just from the screen.
Color indexes are expected to be base 1 like the collections (unverified).
The document palette (Type cdrDocumentPalette) is saved inside the .cdr, not as a separate file (unverified that FileName is empty for it).
cards.example:
Dim pal As Palette
Set pal = Palettes.Create("Brand 2026", , True)
pal.AddColor CreateCMYKColor(0, 90, 85, 0)
pal.AddColor CreateCMYKColor(100, 70, 0, 20)
pal.AddColor CreateRGBColor(245, 240, 230)
pal.Save
Debug.Print pal.ColorCount, pal.FileName
cards.source: cdr_api_22 agent (VGCoreAuto.tlb harvest; coclass members read from the members_on interface IVGPalette)

cards.name: PaletteManager
cards.summary: Application-level access to every color palette CorelDRAW has loaded, open on screen or not, plus the default palette and loading palettes from files. Wider than Palettes, which only covers palettes open on screen.
use_for: find a palette by name or file whether or not it is shown
load a client palette file for a color-matching macro
read the default palette that new documents use
avoid: creating new palettes here: PaletteManager has no Create; use Palettes.Create / CreateFromDocument / CreateFromSelection
cards.how: Coclass; members are on IVGPaletteManager. Reach it as Application.PaletteManager. GetPalette takes an index, unique ID, name or file name. For Each iterates the loaded palettes; call LoadAllPalettes first to include every registered palette.

key_members.name: GetPalette
key_members.use: palette by index, unique ID, name or file name

key_members.name: OpenPalettes
key_members.use: the Palettes collection of palettes shown on screen

key_members.name: LoadPalette
key_members.use: load a palette file and return it

key_members.name: LoadAllPalettes
key_members.use: load every palette registered with CorelDRAW

gotchas: PaletteCount and For Each only see loaded palettes; call LoadAllPalettes to see the full library (it may be slow with large libraries, unverified).
GetPalette with a name that matches nothing raises an error or returns Nothing (unverified which).
cards.example:
Dim pal As Palette
PaletteManager.LoadAllPalettes
For Each pal In PaletteManager
    Debug.Print pal.Name, pal.ColorCount, pal.IsOpen
Next pal
Debug.Print PaletteManager.DefaultPalette.Name
cards.source: cdr_api_22 agent (VGCoreAuto.tlb harvest; coclass members read from the members_on interface IVGPaletteManager)

cards.name: Palettes
cards.summary: The color palettes currently open on screen, plus the factory calls that open palette files, open fixed libraries (PANTONE, TRUMATCH ...) and create new palettes from scratch, from the document or from the selection.
use_for: create a client palette from the colors used in a finished logo (CreateFromDocument / CreateFromSelection)
open a PANTONE library for spot-color matching
open a palette file shipped with a brand kit
avoid: looking for a palette that is loaded but not shown: use PaletteManager.GetPalette
cards.how: Coclass; members are on IVGPalettes. Reach it as Application.Palettes (or PaletteManager.OpenPalettes). Item is base 1 by index or by name. OpenFixed takes a cdrPaletteID such as cdrPANTONECoated.

key_members.name: Item
key_members.use: open palette by base-1 index or name

key_members.name: OpenFixed
key_members.use: open a fixed library by cdrPaletteID

key_members.name: Create
key_members.use: new empty custom palette (Name, FileName, Overwrite)

key_members.name: CreateFromDocument
key_members.use: palette of the colors used in the document

key_members.name: CreateFromSelection
key_members.use: palette of the colors in the selected shapes

gotchas: Create / CreateFromDocument with a name that already exists fails unless Overwrite is True (unverified error text).
CreateFromSelection reads the current selection; select the shapes first (ActiveSelection), or the palette comes out empty (unverified).
cards.example:
Dim pal As Palette
Set pal = Palettes.CreateFromSelection("Logo colors", , True)
Debug.Print pal.Name, pal.ColorCount
Set pal = Palettes.OpenFixed(cdrPANTONECoated)
Debug.Print Palettes.Count
cards.source: cdr_api_22 agent (VGCoreAuto.tlb harvest; coclass members read from the members_on interface IVGPalettes)

cards.name: PatternCanvas
cards.summary: The pixel grid of a two-color bitmap pattern (the 1-bit tile used by two-color pattern fills): size, individual pixels and simple drawing operations. Front and back colors come from the PatternFill, not from the canvas.
use_for: generate a custom two-color tile (stripes, checks, dots) for a screen-print or textile mock-up
read or tweak the tile of an existing two-color pattern fill
avoid: full-color or vector patterns: those come from files through PatternFill.Load / Fill.ApplyPatternFill with a FileName
fine artwork: the canvas is a small 1-bit grid (16, 32, 64 px or custom)
cards.how: Coclass; members are on IVGPatternCanvas. Make one with Application.CreatePatternCanvas, read one from Shape.Fill.Pattern.Canvas, or take a preset from Application.PatternCanvases.Item(i). Assign it back to PatternFill.Canvas to use it.

key_members.name: Pixel
key_members.use: on/off state of the pixel at (x, y)

key_members.name: FillArea
key_members.use: set a rectangle of pixels on (or off with State False)

key_members.name: CopyArea
key_members.use: copy a pixel rectangle to a new origin

key_members.name: Select
key_members.use: load a preset tile by index

key_members.name: PutCopy
key_members.use: copy another canvas into this one

key_members.name: Data
key_members.use: the whole canvas as a string (save / restore)

gotchas: Pixel coordinates are whole numbers; whether they start at 0 or 1 is not in the harvest (unverified).
Changing the Canvas object read from a fill may not update the fill until it is assigned back to PatternFill.Canvas (unverified).
PSet and Line take Step / Flags and Color arguments whose meaning is not documented in the harvest (unverified); FillArea is the safer way to draw.
cards.example:
Dim cv As PatternCanvas
Set cv = CreatePatternCanvas
cv.Size = cdrPatternCanvas16x16
cv.Clear
cv.FillArea 0, 0, 7, 7, True
cv.FillArea 8, 8, 15, 15, True
ActiveShape.Fill.ApplyPatternFill cdrTwoColorPattern
ActiveShape.Fill.Pattern.Canvas = cv
cards.source: cdr_api_22 agent (VGCoreAuto.tlb harvest; coclass members read from the members_on interface IVGPatternCanvas)

cards.name: PatternCanvases
cards.summary: The application's list of two-color pattern tiles offered in the two-color pattern picker. Scripts read tiles from it and add their own so they can be applied by index.
use_for: register a generated two-color tile so ApplyPatternFill can use it by PatternCanvasIndex
list the stock two-color tiles for a pattern swatch sheet
avoid: storing full-color or vector patterns: this list holds only two-color canvases
cards.how: Coclass; members are on IVGPatternCanvases. Reach it as Application.PatternCanvases. Item is base 1 and writable; Add returns the new index, which Fill.ApplyPatternFill accepts as PatternCanvasIndex.

key_members.name: Item
key_members.use: tile by base-1 index (get or set)

key_members.name: Add
key_members.use: add a PatternCanvas and return its index

gotchas: The list is application-wide; whether added tiles persist to the next session is not in the harvest (unverified).
Removing a tile shifts the indexes of later tiles; macros that stored indexes break.
cards.example:
Dim cv As PatternCanvas, i As Long
Set cv = CreatePatternCanvas
cv.Size = cdrPatternCanvas16x16
cv.FillArea 0, 0, 15, 3, True
i = PatternCanvases.Add(cv)
ActiveShape.Fill.ApplyPatternFill cdrTwoColorPattern, , i
cards.source: cdr_api_22 agent (VGCoreAuto.tlb harvest; coclass members read from the members_on interface IVGPatternCanvases)

cards.name: PatternFill
cards.summary: The settings of a pattern fill on a shape: pattern type (two-color, full-color / vector, bitmap), colors for two-color tiles, the tile canvas or source file, tile size, origin, row/column offset, skew, rotation, mirroring and whether the pattern transforms with the shape.
use_for: tile a texture or brand motif across a background shape
set tile size and rotation of a fabric or wallpaper pattern mock-up
recolor a two-color pattern to brand colors
lock a pattern so it scales and rotates with the object
avoid: reading Pattern on a shape whose Fill.Type is not a pattern fill: check Fill.Type first
photo textures that must not repeat: use a bitmap PowerClip instead
cards.how: Coclass; members are on IVGPatternFill. Apply with Shape.Fill.ApplyPatternFill(Type, FileName, PatternCanvasIndex, FrontColor, EndColor, TransformWithShape), then read or adjust Shape.Fill.Pattern. Tile sizes and origin are in document units, angles in degrees.

key_members.name: FrontColor
key_members.use: foreground color of a two-color pattern

key_members.name: BackColor
key_members.use: background color of a two-color pattern

key_members.name: Canvas
key_members.use: the two-color tile as a PatternCanvas

key_members.name: TileOffset
key_members.use: row / column offset for a brick layout (percent of tile, unverified unit)

key_members.name: TransformWithShape
key_members.use: pattern follows the shape's scale / rotate / skew

gotchas: The harvest lists three kinds (two-color bitmap, full-color bitmap, vector) but the enum is cdrTwoColorPattern / cdrFullColorPattern / cdrBitmapPattern; cdrFullColorPattern is taken here to be the vector pattern and cdrBitmapPattern the full-color bitmap (unverified mapping).
FrontColor / BackColor only matter for two-color patterns.
TileWidth / TileHeight follow ActiveDocument.Unit.
Without TransformWithShape, scaling the shape changes how many tiles show instead of scaling them.
cards.example:
Dim pf As PatternFill
ActiveShape.Fill.ApplyPatternFill cdrTwoColorPattern
Set pf = ActiveShape.Fill.Pattern
pf.FrontColor.CMYKAssign 0, 90, 85, 0
pf.BackColor.CMYKAssign 0, 0, 0, 0
pf.TileWidth = 5: pf.TileHeight = 5
pf.RotationAngle = 45
pf.TransformWithShape = True
cards.source: cdr_api_22 agent (VGCoreAuto.tlb harvest; coclass members read from the members_on interface IVGPatternFill)

review.changes: key_members: marked the TileOffset percent unit as unverified

cards.name: PDFVBASettings
cards.summary: The Publish to PDF settings of a document: page range, PDF version / PDF/X standard, color mode and profile, font embedding, bitmap compression and downsampling, bleed and printer marks, overprints, hyperlinks, bookmarks and security. Used with Document.PublishToPDF to make print or web PDFs from a script.
use_for: publish a press-ready PDF/X-4 with 3 mm bleed and crop marks
make a small web PDF with JPEG compression and downsampled images
export a page range of a catalog as a client proof
batch-publish many .cdr files with one saved PDF style
avoid: raster exports (PNG / JPG): use Document.Export or ExportBitmap
relying on settings left over from an earlier publish: call Reset or Load a named style first
cards.how: Coclass; members are on IPDFVBASettings. Reach it as ActiveDocument.PDFSettings, set its properties, then call ActiveDocument.PublishToPDF(FileName). Load / Save use named PDF styles (the presets in the Publish to PDF dialog); ShowDialog opens that dialog for a human.

key_members.name: Save
key_members.use: save the current settings as a named style

key_members.name: PublishRange
key_members.use: whole document, current page, selection or page range (pdfExportRange)

key_members.name: PageRange
key_members.use: page list such as "1-3,5" when PublishRange is pdfPageRange

key_members.name: pdfVersion
key_members.use: Acrobat version or PDF/X / PDF/A standard

key_members.name: BitmapCompression
key_members.use: none, LZW, JPEG, ZIP or JPEG 2000

key_members.name: IncludeBleed
key_members.use: extend output past the page edge

key_members.name: Bleed
key_members.use: bleed amount in tens of microns

gotchas: Bleed is an integer in tens of microns (harvest description): 3 mm = 300, not 3.
Settings live on the document object for the session; a second publish inherits the first one's choices unless Reset or Load is called (unverified that they are also saved in the .cdr).
PageRange is used only when PublishRange = pdfPageRange.
The harvest descriptions of EmbedFile (bool) and EmbedFilename (string) look swapped; trust the types.
OpenPassword / PermissionPassword write passwords into the macro; keep them out of shared scripts.
cards.example:
With ActiveDocument.PDFSettings
    .Reset
    .PublishRange = pdfWholeDocument
    .pdfVersion = pdfVersionPDFX4
    .IncludeBleed = True: .Bleed = 300
    .CropMarks = True
End With
ActiveDocument.PublishToPDF "C:\out\poster.pdf"

cards.name: Point
cards.summary: A 2D point (x, y) with vector add / subtract and distance. A geometry helper used by curve, segment and math calls, not a visible object.
use_for: measure the distance between two anchor positions in a layout macro
sample a position along a path (Segment.GetPointAt) to place labels or icons
build point lists for generated curves
avoid: placing shapes: Point does not draw anything; create shapes on a Layer
cards.how: Coclass; members are on IVGPoint. Create one with Application.Math.CreatePoint(x, y); get them from Segment.GetPointAt, SubPath.GetPointAt, PointRange.Item / First / Last, Properties.GetPoint and the Math helpers (MidPoint, Interpolate, ClosestPointToLineSegment).

key_members.name: Add
key_members.use: move the point by a Vector

key_members.name: Subtract
key_members.use: move the point back by a Vector

key_members.name: BindToDocument
key_members.use: use the document's coordinate system and units

gotchas: A point that is not bound to a document may not be in the document's units (harvest: BindToDocument 'makes it use the coordinates in the document's coordinate system'); bind it before mixing with page positions.
Add / Subtract change the point in place; take GetCopy first to keep the original.
CorelDRAW y grows upward, unlike screen coordinates.
cards.example:
Dim a As Point, b As Point
Set a = Application.Math.CreatePoint(0, 0)
Set b = Application.Math.CreatePoint(3, 4)
a.BindToDocument ActiveDocument
b.BindToDocument ActiveDocument
Debug.Print a.DistanceTo(b)
cards.source: cdr_api_22 agent (VGCoreAuto.tlb harvest; coclass members read from the members_on interface IVGPoint)

cards.name: PointRange
cards.summary: An ordered, editable list of points with add / insert / remove, reverse, de-duplicate and smoothing. Used to build curves from coordinates and to receive evenly spaced points sampled along a path.
use_for: draw a chart line or route from data coordinates
scatter icons evenly along a path (SubPath.GetEvenlySpacedPoints)
smooth a jittery hand-drawn or traced polyline
avoid: one point: use Point
editing an existing curve's nodes: work on Curve.Nodes / Segments instead
cards.how: Coclass; members are on IVGPointRange. Create with Application.Math.CreatePointRange; also returned by SubPath.GetEvenlySpacedPoints. Turn it into a curve with Curve.AppendSubpathFromPoints(Points, Close) or AppendSubpathFitToPoints, then Layer.CreateCurve(curve). Item is base 1.

key_members.name: AddPointXY
key_members.use: append a point from x, y

key_members.name: InsertPoint
key_members.use: insert a point at an index

key_members.name: Smoothen
key_members.use: smooth the points over a window (Closed for loops)

gotchas: Like Point, an unbound range may not use document units; BindToDocument before mixing with page coordinates (unverified what the unbound unit is).
Smoothen changes the points in place; GetCopy first to keep the raw data.
cards.example:
Dim pr As PointRange, crv As Curve
Set pr = Application.Math.CreatePointRange
pr.AddPointXY 0, 0: pr.AddPointXY 2, 1.5: pr.AddPointXY 4, 0.5
Set crv = Application.CreateCurve(ActiveDocument)
crv.AppendSubpathFromPoints pr, False
ActiveLayer.CreateCurve crv
cards.source: cdr_api_22 agent (VGCoreAuto.tlb harvest; coclass members read from the members_on interface IVGPointRange)

cards.name: Polygon
cards.summary: The live properties of a polygon or star shape drawn with the Polygon / Star tools: whether it is a polygon, star or polygon-as-star, the number of sides (points), and star sharpness.
use_for: generate badges, seals and starbursts with an exact number of points
restyle every star on a page to the same point count and sharpness
avoid: shapes already converted to curves: they have no Polygon properties; edit nodes instead

equivalents.AI: Adobe Shape Construction Regular Polygon Tool

cards.how: Coclass; members are on IVGPolygon. Reach it as Shape.Polygon on a shape whose Type is cdrPolygonShape. Create polygons with ActiveLayer.CreatePolygon2(CenterX, CenterY, Radius, Sides, Angle, InnerRadius, Star, Sharpness) or CreatePolygon(Left, Top, Right, Bottom, Sides ...).

key_members.name: Sides
key_members.use: number of sides or star points

key_members.name: Sharpness
key_members.use: how deep the star points are cut

gotchas: Shape.Polygon is only meaningful when Shape.Type = cdrPolygonShape; on other shapes it errors or returns Nothing (unverified which).
Sharpness has no visible effect on a plain cdrPolygon (unverified).
ConvertToCurves removes the live polygon; later changes to Sides are impossible.
cards.example:
Dim s As Shape
Set s = ActiveLayer.CreatePolygon2(4, 4, 2, 5)
s.Polygon.Type = cdrStar
s.Polygon.Sides = 12
s.Polygon.Sharpness = 30
s.Fill.UniformColor.CMYKAssign 0, 20, 100, 0

cards.name: PostScriptFill
cards.summary: The settings of a PostScript texture fill on a shape (the procedural textures in the PostScript Fill list, such as bricks, waves or crosshatch): which texture and its up to five numeric parameters.
use_for: procedural line or dot textures for screen-print or engraving artwork
vintage halftone-style backgrounds that stay vector in PostScript output
avoid: output that is not PostScript-based (web, office printers): use a pattern fill or bitmap texture instead (unverified how each non-PostScript export renders it)
guessing what Param1-5 mean: they differ per texture
cards.how: Coclass; members are on IVGPostScriptFill. Apply with Shape.Fill.ApplyPostscriptFill(IndexOrName), then read or change Shape.Fill.PostScript. Select switches texture by index or name; SetProperties sets up to five texture parameters in order.

key_members.name: Select
key_members.use: switch texture by index or name

key_members.name: Properties
key_members.use: texture parameter number Index (get or set)

key_members.name: SetProperties
key_members.use: set up to five parameters in one call

gotchas: Each texture has its own parameter list (frequency, line width, gray levels ...); the harvest does not name them, so read Properties(i) from a fill set up in the UI first (unverified meanings).
PostScript textures may render exactly only on a PostScript device; screen and raster output may differ (unverified).
Texture names come from the installed list; a name that does not exist fails (unverified error).
The index base of Properties(Index) is not in the harvest (unverified: the example assumes 1).
cards.example:
ActiveShape.Fill.ApplyPostscriptFill 1
With ActiveShape.Fill.PostScript
    Debug.Print .Index, .Name, .Properties(1), .Properties(2)
    .SetProperties 20, 5
End With

cards.name: PowerClip
cards.summary: The contents of a PowerClip container: shapes placed inside another shape and clipped to it (CorelDRAW's clipping mask / frame). Gives access to the clipped shapes, the lock between frame and contents, edit mode and extraction.
use_for: place a product photo inside a circle or brand frame
fill text or a logo with an image
batch-swap the photos inside template frames
pull contents out of frames before a print handoff
avoid: calling PowerClip on a shape that has no contents: check Shape.PowerClip for Nothing first (unverified)
simple crops of a bitmap: Bitmap cropping or Shape.Bitmap.Crop may be lighter (unverified)
cards.how: Coclass; members are on IVGPowerClip. Put content in with content.AddToPowerClip(frame, CenterInContainer) (IVGShape or IVGShapeRange), then reach the container's contents as frame.PowerClip; Document.ActivePowerClip is the one in edit mode. Shapes lists what is inside; ExtractShapes takes it all out.

key_members.name: ContentsLocked
key_members.use: contents move with the frame when True

key_members.name: ExtractShapes
key_members.use: take the contents out and return them

gotchas: CenterInContainer of AddToPowerClip is a cdrTriState with default -2 (cdrUndefined): pass cdrTrue or cdrFalse explicitly or the user's preference decides centering.
EnterEditMode changes UI state; always pair it with LeaveEditMode or later macros run inside the PowerClip (unverified).
Shape.PowerClip on a shape with no contents returns Nothing (unverified).
cards.example:
Dim photo As Shape, frame As Shape
Set photo = ActivePage.FindShape("photo")
Set frame = ActivePage.FindShape("frame")
photo.AddToPowerClip frame, cdrTrue
frame.PowerClip.ContentsLocked = True
Debug.Print frame.PowerClip.Shapes.Count
cards.source: cdr_api_22 agent (VGCoreAuto.tlb harvest; coclass members read from the members_on interface IVGPowerClip)

cards.name: PrintDocuments
cards.summary: The read-only list of documents queued in the application's print job (PrintJob.Documents). Only a count and per-item access.
use_for: check which documents a combined print job holds before PrintOut
avoid: adding documents here: use PrintJob.AddDocument
cards.how: Coclass; members are on IPrnVBAPrintDocuments. Reach it as Application.PrintJob.Documents. Item returns an IPrnVBAPrintDocument, whose members were not harvested.
gotchas: The IPrnVBAPrintDocument items have no harvested members, so the list is mostly useful for its Count.

cards.example:
With PrintJob
    .Clear
    .AddDocument ActiveDocument, "1-2"
    Debug.Print .Documents.Count, .Pages.Count
End With

cards.name: Printer
cards.summary: One installed printer as CorelDRAW sees it: name, driver, port, whether it is the default, ready, PostScript-capable and color-capable, plus its properties dialog.
use_for: pick a PostScript printer for separations or in-RIP trapping
check a printer is ready before an unattended print run
list printers for a print-dispatch macro
avoid: choosing the printer by assigning this object when only the name is known: PrintSettings.SelectPrinter(Name) is simpler
cards.how: Coclass; members are on IPrnVBAPrinter. Reach printers through Application.Printers (Item, Count, Default) or the one chosen for a document as ActiveDocument.PrintSettings.Printer.

key_members.name: Default
key_members.use: True for the system default printer

key_members.name: Ready
key_members.use: True when the printer is ready

key_members.name: ColorEnabled
key_members.use: True when color output is enabled

gotchas: ShowDialog is modal: an unattended script hangs until someone closes it.
PostScript-only features (separations screening, in-RIP trapping, PrintPostScript settings) need PostScriptEnabled = True (unverified that CorelDRAW blocks them otherwise).
cards.example:
Dim i As Long
For i = 1 To Printers.Count
    With Printers.Item(i)
        Debug.Print .Name, .PostScriptEnabled, .ColorEnabled, .Ready
    End With
Next i
Debug.Print Printers.Default.Name

cards.name: PrintJob
cards.summary: An application-level print job that collects pages from one or more documents and prints them in one go with one set of print settings.
use_for: print selected pages from several open documents as one job (proof pack, imposition test)
send a batch of client proofs to one printer with shared settings
avoid: printing one document: ActiveDocument.PrintSettings plus PrintOut is shorter
cards.how: Coclass; members are on IPrnVBAPrintJob. Reach it as Application.PrintJob. Clear it, add pages with AddDocument(Document, PageRange) or AddPage(Page), set Settings, then PrintOut.

key_members.name: AddDocument
key_members.use: add a document or a page range of it

key_members.name: PrintOut
key_members.use: send the job to the printer

gotchas: The job is shared at application level; clear it first or pages from an earlier macro go out too (unverified that it persists between macros).
PrintOut really prints (or writes a file when Settings.PrintToFile is True); test with a PDF printer.
cards.example:
With PrintJob
    .Clear
    .AddDocument Documents(1), "1"
    .AddPage Documents(2).Pages.Item(2)
    .Settings.SelectPrinter "Microsoft Print to PDF"
    .PrintOut
End With
cards.source: cdr_api_22 agent (VGCoreAuto.tlb harvest; coclass members read from the members_on interface IPrnVBAPrintJob)

cards.name: PrintLayout
cards.summary: The layout part of print settings: bleed limit, tiling of oversized pages across sheets with overlap and tiling marks, and where the page sits on the printer sheet (as in document, fit, centered, corners, custom).
use_for: tile a large poster or banner across A4 / A3 sheets with overlap
fit-to-page proofs of oversized artwork
print with a bleed limit so bleed shows on proofs
avoid: setting paper size here: use PrintSettings.SetPaperSize / SetCustomPaperSize
cards.how: Coclass; members are on IPrnVBAPrintLayout. Reach it as ActiveDocument.PrintSettings.Layout (or PrintJob.Settings.Layout). Placement takes a PrnPlaceType such as prnPlaceFitToPage or prnPlaceCenterPage.

key_members.name: Placement
key_members.use: where the page sits on the sheet (PrnPlaceType)

gotchas: TileOverlap and BleedLimit units are not given in the harvest (unverified: document units).
prnPlaceFitToPage scales the artwork; do not use it for final-size proofs.
cards.example:
With ActiveDocument.PrintSettings.Layout
    .PrintTiledPages = True
    .TileOverlap = 10
    .PrintTilingMarks = True
    .Placement = prnPlaceAsInDocument
End With

cards.name: PrintOptions
cards.summary: Miscellaneous print settings: which object kinds print (vectors, bitmaps, text), text in black, color mode and color profile use, bitmap downsampling, page rasterization, fountain steps, preserving pure black, and the job information sheet.
use_for: print a text-only proofreading copy (PrintBitmaps off)
rasterize complex transparency pages to avoid printer RIP errors
print grayscale proofs of a color layout
add a job info sheet to a print run
avoid: printer marks and crop marks: those are on PrintPrepress
separation settings: PrintSeparations
cards.how: Coclass; members are on IPrnVBAPrintOptions. Reach it as ActiveDocument.PrintSettings.Options (or PrintJob.Settings.Options).

key_members.name: ObjectsColorMode
key_members.use: color mode all objects are output as

key_members.name: RasterizePage
key_members.use: rasterize the whole page before sending

gotchas: RasterizePage turns vectors and text into pixels on output; keep RasterizeResolution at device resolution or text gets soft.
Low FountainSteps shows banding in gradients on press.
cards.example:
With ActiveDocument.PrintSettings.Options
    .PrintBitmaps = False
    .TextInBlack = True
    .PreservePureBlack = True
    .FountainSteps = 256
End With

cards.name: PrintPages
cards.summary: The read-only list of pages queued in the application's print job (PrintJob.Pages): a count and per-page access.
use_for: confirm the page count of a combined print job before sending it
avoid: adding pages here: use PrintJob.AddPage or AddDocument
cards.how: Coclass; members are on IPrnVBAPrintPages. Reach it as Application.PrintJob.Pages. Item returns an IPrnVBAPrintPage, whose members were not harvested.
gotchas: IPrnVBAPrintPage has no harvested members; use Count as the check.
Item index base is not in the harvest (unverified: 1).

With PrintJob
    .Clear
    .AddPage ActivePage
    Debug.Print .Pages.Count
End With

cards.name: PrintPostScript
cards.summary: PostScript output settings for printing: PostScript level, DSC conformance, JPEG compression of bitmaps, font download and TrueType conversion, OPI / DCS links, curve complexity and flatness, fountain-step handling, screen frequency, and PDF-related options for distilled output.
use_for: make PostScript files for an older RIP (Level 2, DSC-conformant)
avoid limitcheck errors on complex curves by limiting points per curve and raising flatness
set the halftone screen frequency for a PostScript proofer
avoid: non-PostScript printers: these settings apply to PostScript output only (unverified that they are ignored otherwise)
cards.how: Coclass; members are on IPrnVBAPrintPostScript. Reach it as ActiveDocument.PrintSettings.PostScript (or PrintJob.Settings.PostScript).

key_members.name: TrueTypeToType1
key_members.use: convert TrueType to Type 1 before download

key_members.name: OptimizeFountainFills
key_members.use: lower fountain steps for short fills

key_members.name: AutoIncreaseFountainSteps
key_members.use: raise fountain steps for long fills

gotchas: Raising Flatness makes curves visibly faceted at large sizes; use it only to get past RIP errors.
Level and JPEG settings must match what the RIP supports; Level 3 features fail on Level 2 devices (unverified behaviour per device).
cards.example:
With ActiveDocument.PrintSettings.PostScript
    .ConformToDSC = True
    .MaxPointsPerCurve = 2000
    .AutoIncreaseFlatness = True
    .ScreenFrequency = 150
End With

cards.name: PrintPrepress
cards.summary: Prepress marks and film options for printing: crop / fold marks, registration marks and their style, color calibration bar, densitometer scale, file information and page numbers, job name slug, negative and mirrored output.
use_for: add crop and registration marks to press proofs
print film negatives or emulsion-down output for screen printing
slug every proof with job name and page numbers
avoid: PDF output marks: PDFVBASettings has its own CropMarks / RegistrationMarks
cards.how: Coclass; members are on IPrnVBAPrintPrepress. Reach it as ActiveDocument.PrintSettings.Prepress (or PrintJob.Settings.Prepress).

key_members.name: Densities
key_members.use: density value at Index for the scale

key_members.name: InfoWithinPage
key_members.use: place info inside the page area

key_members.name: MarksToObjects
key_members.use: place marks around the objects instead of the page

gotchas: Marks need paper larger than the page; on same-size paper they are cut off (unverified whether CorelDRAW warns).
Invert and Mirror are for film / screen-print output; leaving them on ruins normal proofs.
cards.example:
With ActiveDocument.PrintSettings.Prepress
    .CropMarks = True
    .RegistrationMarks = True
    .ColorCalibrationBar = True
    .FileInfo = True
    .JobName = "Client X - poster v3"
End With

cards.summary: Color separation print settings: turn separations on, print plates in color, hexachrome, convert spots to CMYK, empty plates, overprint handling, automatic spreading (trapping), imaging resolution, screen frequency, halftone dot and screening technology, and the plate list.
use_for: print one plate per ink for screen printing or offset film
convert stray spot colors to process for a CMYK-only job

avoid: PDF separations: publish a composite PDF and let the RIP separate
in-RIP trapping settings: PrintTrapping

key_members.name: InColor
key_members.use: print each plate in its ink color

key_members.name: EmptyPlates
key_members.use: print plates with nothing on them

key_members.name: AutoSpreadTextAbove
key_members.use: smallest text size that gets trapped

gotchas: BasicScreen, HalftoneType and ScreenTechnology are strings that must match names the printer / PPD offers (unverified list).
AlwaysOverprintBlack also overprints large black areas, which can show objects beneath through the black.
cards.example:
With ActiveDocument.PrintSettings.Separations
    .Enabled = True
    .SpotToCMYK = True
    .AlwaysOverprintBlack = True

End With

key_members.use: save settings as a print style

key_members.name: PrintToFile
key_members.use: write to a file instead of the device

key_members.name: PrintRange
key_members.use: whole document, current page, selection or page range

gotchas: PrintOut prints for real; route tests to a PDF printer or PrintToFile.
ShowDialog is modal and blocks an unattended run.
PageRange is read only when PrintRange = prnPageRange.
cards.example:
With ActiveDocument.PrintSettings
    .Reset
    .SelectPrinter "Microsoft Print to PDF"

    .PageRange = "1-2"

End With

use_for: offset jobs where the RIP must trap adjacent spot or process colors

avoid: devices without in-RIP trapping (unverified: PostScript 3 devices with trapping support)
simple overprint fixes: AlwaysOverprintBlack / AutoSpreading on PrintSeparations

key_members.use: how far one color spreads into another

key_members.name: BlackColorLimit
key_members.use: black ink density counted as pure black

The example values 0.003 / 0.005 assume inches (unverified); check Width after setting it.

With ActiveDocument.PrintSettings.Trapping

cards.name: ProofColorSettings

flag out-of-gamut brand colors before sending to print
print or export a hard proof that simulates the press profile

Make one with Application.CreateProofColorSettings(ProfileName, RenderingIntent, PreserveColorValues); the live view's settings are ActiveWindow.ActiveView.ProofColorSettings; export options carry one in StructExportOptions.ProofColorSettings; PrintSettings.PrintColorProof(ProofSettings) prints with one.

key_members.name: PreserveColorValues
key_members.use: keep numbers when no model conversion is needed

Dim pcs As ProofColorSettings

cards.name: Properties
cards.summary: A hidden key-value store attached to a document, page, layer or shape (or to the application session): values are addressed by a section name plus a numeric ID and are saved with the file. Also stores files, points, vectors and curves.
use_for: tag template placeholders with a role (headline, price, photo) so a fill macro can find them
remember the source data row a generated shape came from
store per-document pipeline state (version, client id) inside the .cdr
keep macro settings between runs (Application.GlobalUserData)
avoid: data a designer should see or edit: use Object Data fields (Shape.ObjectData / DataFields)
large binaries in every shape: PutFile on many shapes bloats the file (unverified size impact)
cards.how: Coclass; members are on IVGProperties. Reach it as Shape.Properties, Page.Properties, Layer.Properties, Document.Properties, Application.GlobalUserData / SessionUserData, or Application.CreateProperties for a free-standing set. Item(Name, ID) gets or sets a variant; Name is a section string, ID a long.

key_members.name: Item
key_members.use: get or set the value at (Name, ID)

key_members.name: DeleteAll
key_members.use: remove every item of a section name

key_members.name: Description
key_members.use: read the name and ID at a position

key_members.name: GetFile
key_members.use: write a stored file back to disk

key_members.name: SetPoint
key_members.use: store a Point under a UUID name

gotchas: Use a distinctive section Name (for example your tool's name) to avoid clashing with other macros' data.
Reading Item for a key that does not exist raises an error (unverified); test with Exists first.
SessionUserData lasts only while CorelDRAW runs; GlobalUserData is meant to persist across sessions (unverified where it is stored).
Whether Properties travel with a shape when it is duplicated or copied to another document is not in the harvest (unverified).

Dim s As Shape
Set s = ActiveShape
s.Properties.Item("PGD", 1) = "headline"
If s.Properties.Exists("PGD", 1) Then
    Debug.Print s.Properties.Item("PGD", 1)
End If
ActiveDocument.Properties.Item("PGD", 1) = "v3"

cards.name: PSScreenOptions
cards.summary: The PostScript halftone screen of one object's fill or outline: screen (dot) type, angle and frequency in lines per inch. This is the object-level 'PostScript Options' halftone setting used when the object is output to PostScript.
use_for: give a spot-color object a coarse decorative line or dot screen on film
set a specific screen angle to avoid moire on a spot plate
avoid: whole-job screening: set it on PrintSeparations / PrintPostScript
non-PostScript output: the screen is not applied there (unverified)
cards.how: Coclass; members are on IVGPSScreenOptions. Reach it as Shape.Fill.PSScreen or Shape.Outline.PSScreen. Select or SetProperties(IndexOrName, Angle, Frequency) picks the screen type; NameByIndex lists the available types.

key_members.name: Frequency
key_members.use: screen frequency in lines per inch

key_members.name: Select
key_members.use: choose a screen type by index or name

key_members.name: SetProperties
key_members.use: type, angle and frequency in one call

key_members.name: NameByIndex
key_members.use: name of screen type n (empty when n is out of range)

gotchas: In CorelDRAW the object-level halftone screen is offered for spot-color fills and outlines; on process colors it may have no effect (unverified).
UserAssign opens a modal dialog and blocks an unattended run.
cards.example:
Dim ps As PSScreenOptions, i As Long
Set ps = ActiveShape.Fill.PSScreen
For i = 0 To 10
    Debug.Print i, ps.NameByIndex(i)
Next i
ps.SetProperties ps.NameByIndex(1), 45, 30
cards.source: cdr_api_22 agent (VGCoreAuto.tlb harvest; coclass members read from the members_on interface IVGPSScreenOptions)

cards.name: RecentFile
cards.summary: One entry of CorelDRAW's recent-files list (File > Open Recent): its name, folder and full path, its position, and calls to open it or remove it from the list.
use_for: reopen the last edited client file at the start of a session macro
clean stale network paths out of the recent list
avoid: deleting the file itself: Delete only removes the list entry
cards.how: Coclass; members are on IVGRecentFile. Reach it as Application.RecentFiles.Item(i) or as the result of RecentFiles.Add(Name, Path).

key_members.name: Delete
key_members.use: remove the entry from the list

gotchas: Open on an entry whose file was moved or deleted raises an error (unverified); check the path with Dir first.
Open returns a generic IDispatch; assign it to a Document variable.
Name / Path / FullName are writable but only change the list entry, not the file on disk.
cards.example:
Dim d As Document
If RecentFiles.Count > 0 Then
    Debug.Print RecentFiles.Item(1).FullName
    Set d = RecentFiles.Item(1).Open
End If
cards.source: cdr_api_22 agent (VGCoreAuto.tlb harvest; coclass members read from the members_on interface IVGRecentFile)

cards.name: RecentFiles
cards.summary: CorelDRAW's most-recently-used file list: count, maximum length, per-entry access and adding entries.
use_for: list recent client files in a session-start dashboard macro
add files a script generated so designers find them in File > Open Recent
avoid: tracking pipeline output: keep your own log file; this list is short and user-facing
cards.how: Coclass; members are on IVGRecentFiles. Reach it as Application.RecentFiles. Item is base 1; Add(Name, Path) adds an entry.

key_members.name: Add
key_members.use: add an entry from name and folder

gotchas: Adding beyond Maximum is expected to push the oldest entry out (unverified).
Whether Path in Add needs a trailing backslash is not in the harvest (unverified); compare FullName of an existing entry.
cards.example:
Dim rf As RecentFile
For Each rf In RecentFiles
    Debug.Print rf.Index, rf.FullName
Next rf
Debug.Print RecentFiles.Count & " of " & RecentFiles.Maximum
cards.source: cdr_api_22 agent (VGCoreAuto.tlb harvest; coclass members read from the members_on interface IVGRecentFiles)

cards.name: Rect
cards.summary: A rectangle value (x, y of the lower-left corner, width, height) with edge and center getters and geometry helpers: intersect, union, offset, inflate, point-in-rect. Used for bounding boxes and for creating rectangles from a box.
use_for: measure the content area of a page before fitting or exporting
check whether two elements overlap in a layout QC macro
draw a background panel with margin around a group (CreateRectangleRect)
align shapes to the edges or center of another object's box
avoid: changing a shape's size by editing its BoundingBox Rect: resize the shape (SetSize / SetBoundingBox) instead
cards.how: Coclass; members are on IVGRect. Make one with Application.CreateRect(x, y, Width, Height); get them from Shape.BoundingBox, ShapeRange.BoundingBox, Page.BoundingBox, Page.GetObjectsBoundingBox, Curve / Segment.BoundingBox. Layer.CreateRectangleRect(Rect) draws one.

key_members.name: Inflate
key_members.use: grow by left, top, right, bottom

gotchas: y is the bottom edge (CorelDRAW y grows upward), so Top = y + Height, unlike screen rectangles (see ScreenRect).
Values follow ActiveDocument.Unit.
Shape.BoundingBox may exclude the outline width; GetBoundingBox has a UseOutline flag when the stroke must count (unverified default).
Intersect of non-overlapping rects comes back empty; test IsEmpty before using it.
cards.example:
Dim r As Rect
Set r = ActivePage.GetObjectsBoundingBox(False, False)
r.Inflate 5, 5, 5, 5
ActiveLayer.CreateRectangleRect r
Debug.Print r.Left, r.Bottom, r.Width, r.Height
cards.source: cdr_api_22 agent (VGCoreAuto.tlb harvest; coclass members read from the members_on interface IVGRect)

cards.name: Rectangle
cards.summary: The live corner properties of a rectangle shape: per-corner roundness or radius, corner type (round, scallop, chamfer), whether corners are equal, the largest possible radius, and relative corner scaling.
use_for: make buttons, cards and badges with exact corner radii
chamfered or scalloped corners for labels and tickets
keep corner radii fixed when a card is resized (RelativeCornerScaling off)
avoid: rectangles converted to curves: no corner properties remain
drawing the rectangle: use Layer.CreateRectangle2 / CreateRectangleRect, then style corners here
cards.how: Coclass; members are on IVGRectangle. Reach it as Shape.Rectangle on a shape whose Type is cdrRectangleShape. Create rectangles with ActiveLayer.CreateRectangle2(x, y, Width, Height, RadiusUL, RadiusUR, RadiusLR, RadiusLL) or CreateRectangle(Left, Top, Right, Bottom, CornerUL ...).
gotchas: Corner* are whole-number roundness values (relative, 0-100 of the maximum, unverified scale) while Radius* are absolute lengths in document units; do not mix them up.
A radius above MaxRadius is clamped or rejected (unverified which).
Shape.Rectangle on a non-rectangle shape errors or returns Nothing (unverified).
cards.example:
Dim s As Shape
ActiveDocument.Unit = cdrMillimeter
Set s = ActiveLayer.CreateRectangle2(0, 0, 85, 55)
s.Rectangle.CornerType = cdrCornerTypeRound
s.Rectangle.SetRadius 3
s.Rectangle.RelativeCornerScaling = False
Debug.Print s.Rectangle.MaxRadius, s.Rectangle.EqualCorners
cards.source: cdr_api_22 agent (VGCoreAuto.tlb harvest; coclass members read from the members_on interface IVGRectangle)

cards.name: Rulers
cards.summary: The ruler units of a document's drawing window: horizontal and vertical ruler unit. Display only.
use_for: switch rulers to pixels for screen work or millimeters for print in a document setup macro
give horizontal and vertical rulers different units for technical drawings
avoid: changing the units a script measures in: that is ActiveDocument.Unit, not the rulers
cards.how: Coclass; members are on IVGRulers. Reach it as ActiveDocument.Rulers. HUnits and VUnits take cdrUnit values.
gotchas: Ruler units and Document.Unit are separate: changing rulers does not change the numbers macros read and write.
Ruler origin and drawing scale are not on this object (not in the harvested members).
cards.example:
With ActiveDocument.Rulers
    .HUnits = cdrMillimeter
    .VUnits = cdrMillimeter
End With
ActiveDocument.Unit = cdrMillimeter
cards.source: cdr_api_22 agent (VGCoreAuto.tlb harvest; coclass members read from the members_on interface IVGRulers)

cards.name: ScreenRect
cards.summary: A rectangle in screen pixels (left, top, width, height, y growing downward) used by the CorelDRAW UI framework for window, docker and view positions, with move, resize, offset, inflate, union and intersect helpers.
use_for: position a custom docker or floating window from a UI add-on
read where a view or dock item sits on screen for UI automation
avoid: document geometry: use Rect, which is in document units with y growing upward
cards.how: Coclass; members are on ICUIScreenRect. Make one with Application.FrameWork.Application.CreateScreenRect(Left, Top, Width, Height); window objects expose theirs as ICUIFrameWindow.Position, ICUIViewWindow.Position, ICUIDockItem.Position, ICUIDockHost.Position and ICUIViewHost.Position.

key_members.name: ReadOnly
key_members.use: True when the rect cannot be changed

gotchas: Screen y grows downward (Top < Bottom), the opposite of Rect.
Any size or position change on a ReadOnly rect fails (harvest description).
Whether changing a window's Position rect moves the window live is not in the harvest (unverified); GetCopy returns a detached copy that never moves anything.
Values are physical pixels; on high-DPI displays they may not match logical pixels (unverified).
cards.example:
Dim sr As ScreenRect
Set sr = Application.FrameWork.Application.CreateScreenRect(100, 100, 400, 300)
sr.Offset 20, 20
Debug.Print sr.Left, sr.Top, sr.Right, sr.Bottom
Debug.Print sr.IsPointInside(150, 150)
cards.source: cdr_api_22 agent (VGCoreAuto.tlb harvest; coclass members read from the members_on interface ICUIScreenRect)

cards.name: Segment
cards.summary: One segment (line or Bezier curve) of a curve between two nodes: its type, length, control handles, and geometry queries at any offset along it (point, tangent, perpendicular, curvature), plus splitting, node insertion and intersections.
use_for: place text, icons or dimension ticks at exact positions along a path
measure path lengths for cutting, sewing or laser jobs
add nodes at fixed intervals before distorting a shape
find where two paths cross
avoid: shapes that are not curves (rectangles, ellipses, text): convert to curves first or read their Curve copy
moving nodes: edit Node objects (StartNode / EndNode or Curve.Nodes)
cards.how: Coclass; members are on IVGSegment. Reach it as Shape.Curve.Segments.Item(i), Curve.SubPaths.Item(n).Segments, or Segment.Next / Previous. Offsets take an OffsetType: cdrRelativeSegmentOffset (0..1 along the segment), cdrAbsoluteSegmentOffset (document units) or cdrParamSegmentOffset (Bezier parameter, the default).

key_members.name: BreakApartAt
key_members.use: split the path at an offset

gotchas: The default OffsetType is cdrParamSegmentOffset (enum value 2), where 0.5 is not the visual midpoint of an uneven Bezier; pass cdrRelativeSegmentOffset for 'halfway along'.
Shape.Curve exists only on curve shapes (Shape.Type = cdrCurveShape); other shapes need ConvertToCurves first or return Nothing (unverified).
AddNodeAt / BreakApartAt change the shape and renumber later segments; loop backwards when inserting.
Angles from GetTangentAt are in degrees (unverified).
cards.example:
Dim seg As Segment, x As Double, y As Double
For Each seg In ActiveShape.Curve.Segments
    seg.GetPointPositionAt x, y, 0.5, cdrRelativeSegmentOffset
    Debug.Print seg.AbsoluteIndex, seg.Type, seg.Length, x, y
Next seg
cards.source: cdr_api_22 agent (VGCoreAuto.tlb harvest; coclass members read from the members_on interface IVGSegment)
